newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Police arrests ex-official in Czech bank fraud.
newsitem.headline: Police arrests ex-official in Czech bank fraud.

text.p: Czech police on Friday arrested one of the five executives of the failed Kreditni Banka AS, Czech papers said on Saturday.
The arrested ex-official is the bank's founding member Milan Nenadl who was still a member of its Board of Directors a month ago, the Czech daily Mlada fronta Dnes wrote.
Nenadl was charged with fraud, damage to creditors, and abetting fraud.
No official was immediately available for comment.
The bank's licence was withdrawn by the Czech National Bank in August with losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns.

The failure of Kreditni Banka, a medium-size bank based in Plzen, West Bohemia, caused a political row over bank supervision and led the government to create a special commission of ministers to lead an investigation into the case.
Kreditni was the 11th of the country's then-over 50 banks to fail.
Kreditni's shareholders, after the central bank shut it in August, voted to liquidate the bank.
Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky said on Friday that the country's banking system was still solid.
